issues.description: Class fields lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents are declared public in the template but the problem UML and the reference solution declare these attributes as private. Specifically: template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java defines "public String lectureName" (line 4) and "public int numberOfInscribedStudents" (line 5); the UML in problem_statement.md (lines 63-68) shows these attributes as private, and the solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java declares them as private (lines 6-10). This visibility mismatch may encourage students to access fields directly instead of implementing the intended encapsulation (private fields with getters/setters), causing confusion about the expected design.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to match the UML and solution: change the visibility of the existing fields to private. For example, in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java make the declarations "private String lectureName;" and "private int numberOfInscribedStudents;". Also ensure the template encourages implementing the remaining attributes and corresponding getters/setters (as specified by the UML) so students follow the intended encapsulation pattern.
